title: Arrays, globals and host I/O: counts and negative errno
summary: Drake's Omega has no heap: arrays are globals, stack arrays from new, or read-only text, and every index and I/O slice is checked. read and write return a count, 0 at end, or minus the Linux errno. I'll show you his partial-read loop that keeps those apart, and how a loop written as while gt k 0 turns a closed stdin into a silent success.
goal: Read stdin with a correct partial-read loop and keep counts, end of input and negative errno distinct.
key_steps: Declare the buffer as a global and name it inside functions, never pass it
Loop on read until it returns 0, adding each partial count
Turn a negative result (minus errno) into a distinct exit status
Cap the input and write the bound proof in a note
Expect trap 3 for a bad slice and error 19 for a global argument

example.code:
note wc.om: count bytes and lines on stdin with a partial-read loop
note proof of the bound: every pass but the last reads at least one byte, and more than CAP
note bytes stops the program, so at most CAP passes read data and one more sees end of input
const CAP ulong 999998
global buf uchar 4096
text lb "bytes "
text ll "lines "
fn putnum v ulong to long
note write v in decimal and a newline. A ulong has at most 20 digits, so bound 20 is proved
d = new uchar 21 0
o = new uchar 21 0
n = ulong 0
x = v
while true bound 20
put d n uchar add rem x 10 48
n = add n 1
x = div x 10
if eq x 0
break
end
end
for i ulong n
put o i get d sub sub n i 1
end
put o n 10
w = write 1 o 0 add n 1
ret w
end
fn main to int
total = ulong 0
lines = ulong 0
done = false
while not done bound 999999
k = read 0 buf 0 len buf
if lt k 0
note a negative result is minus the Linux errno: report it, never treat it as end of input
ret int neg k
end
if eq k 0
done = true
else
n = ulong k
for i ulong n
if eq get buf i 10
lines = add lines 1
end
end
total = add total n
if gt total CAP
ret 3
end
end
end
w = write 1 lb 0 len lb
w = putnum total
w = write 1 ll 0 len ll
w = putnum lines
ret 0
end

common_mistake: Writing while gt k 0, which ends on an error exactly as it ends at end of input. With stdin closed the naive loop printed bytes 0 and exited 0. Handle k < 0 (minus errno) and k == 0 (end) separately, and keep adding partial counts.
evidence_note: Compiled and run on Linux AArch64 with omc befb8199...8a1d with three inputs (short, piped 5000 lines, closed stdin) and three negative controls; reproduced byte for byte. Partial-read counts depend on the kernel pipe; only totals are printed.
